The '''ULTRA''' (Unmanned Long-endurance Tactical Reconnaissance Aircraft) is a developmental [[unmanned aerial vehicle]] (UAV) built by [[Air Force Research Laboratory]] (AFRL) Center for Rapid Innovation (CRI) and DZYNE Technologies Incorporated.

==Background==
Since 2008, the [[U.S. Air Force]]'s primary reconnaissance aircraft has been the [[MQ-9 Reaper]]. However, at a price of $30 million per aircraft, it has been shown to be costly if lost;<ref name="defenseone2july24">[https://www.defenseone.com/technology/2024/07/meet-air-forces-secretive-long-range-drone-flies-days/397816/ Meet the Air Force’s secretive long-range drone that flies for days]. ''Defense One''. 2 July 2024.</ref> during the [[Red Sea crisis]] from October 2023 to May 2025, the [[Houthis]] shot down at least 15 Reapers.<ref>[https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/houthis-shoot-growing-number-us-drones/story?id=121099082 Houthis shoot down growing number of US drones]. ''[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]''. 23 April 2025.</ref> Part of the cost comes from its configuration as a strike UAV, but only a "single-digit percentage" of surveillance missions it flew required a strike capability, so the U.S. Air Force pursued a simpler and cheaper alternative for flying pure [[reconnaissance]] missions.<ref name="defenseone2july24"/><ref>[https://newatlas.com/military/ultra-semi-secret-us-air-force-spy-drone/ Semi-secret US Air Force long-endurance spy drone breaks cover]. ''New Atlas''. 3 July 2024.</ref>

==Design and development==
AFRL's CRI began development of an affordable UAS capable of multi-day duration flights in 2019, going from concept to first flight in less than 10 months.<ref name="ndm12july24">[https://www.nationaldefensemagazine.org/articles/2024/7/12/questions-surround-air-forces-new-gliderbased-drone Questions Surround Air Force’s New Glider-Based Drone]. ''National Defense Magazine''. 12 July 2024.</ref> DZYNE had previously worked on the Long Endurance Aircraft Program (LEAP), which produced an autonomous aircraft deployed in 2016 and could fly for up to 40 hours. This prior experience led to the development of ULTRA, which the Air Force officially started buying in the 2025 budget request, procuring four drones for $35 million.<ref name="defenseone2july24" />

ULTRA is designed to be an [[Intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition, and reconnaissance#Intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance|intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance]] (ISR) truck capable of carrying a variety of [[electro-optical sensor|electro-optical]]/[[infrared camera|infrared]] (EO/IR) and radio frequency (RF), other low-cost intelligence collection payloads, and sensors to provide a reconfigurable platform. 

ULTRA increased endurance and lowered acquisition cost by repurposing the manned [[Stemme S12]] commercial sport [[glider (aircraft)|glider]] and converting it to a military hardened drone using [[commercial-off-the-shelf]] UAV technology, existing manufacturing and supply channels, and limited custom avionics. Lower cost EO/IR and RF sensors are possible due to lower operating altitudes that do not require large optics or high-power RF. It can fly for over 80 hours while carrying over {{cvt|400|lb}} of payload and it has a wingspan of over {{cvt|80|ft}}.<ref name=AFRL>{{cite web|url=https://afresearchlab.com/technology/ultra/|title=Unmanned Long-endurance Tactical Reconnaissance Aircraft (ULTRA)|publisher=Air Force Research Laboratory|access-date=16 May 2024}}</ref><ref name="ndm12july24"/><ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Demarest |first=Colin |date=July 24, 2024 |title=Exclusive: An ULTRA marathon |url=https://www.axios.com/newsletters/axios-future-of-defense-322c8370-4482-11ef-807a-41efc159c674.html}} [[Axios (website)|Axios]].</ref>

Endurance allows these sensors to cover areas with fewer aircraft.<ref name=AFRL/> It has enough range and endurance to loiter for a day over a target after traveling over {{cvt|2,000|mi}}.<ref name="defenseone2july24"/> The aircraft relies on an operator friendly command and control system that allows for "Point and Click" operations. Global operations are possible through satellite-based command and control links that also provide the high-rate ISR data feed to the operators in real time.<ref name=AFRL/>

In May 2024, ''The War Zone'' reported that ULTRA was being operated from [[Al Dhafra Air Base]] in the [[United Arab Emirates]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.twz.com/news-features/air-forces-ultra-long-endurance-glider-like-drone-is-now-operating-in-the-middle-east|publisher=The War Zone|title=Air Force’s ULTRA Long-Endurance Glider-Like Drone Is Now Operating In The Middle East|author1=Joseph Trevithick|author2=Thomans Newdick|date=8 May 2024|access-date=16 May 2024}}</ref> In July 2024, a successful three-day test flight was described to [[Axios (website)|Axios]].<ref name=":0" />
